content.text:
Collapsing the ribbon now hides the tabs too. What's left is one thin row with the primary commands from every tab as small buttons, and every command is marked primary for now. I updated the spec and the code together. 91 of 92 tests pass; the one failure is the palette test that was already failing. `piton check` and `piton build check` pass. I haven't looked at the collapsed row in the running app.

**Collapsed row, left to right:** Open Project | Build Spec | Dark mode, Settings, then the expand chevron at the far right.
- **Buttons:** a small icon beside the label, and Dark mode is a small switch.
- **Dividers:** a thin divider separates commands from different tabs, so Dark mode and Settings (both Application) sit together.
- **Unchanged behaviour:** tooltips, disabled states and the building spinner work as in the full ribbon.

**Changes to how collapsing works:**
- **Expanding:** with the tabs gone, the chevron or Ctrl/Cmd+F1 are the only ways to expand. Clicking a tab to expand is gone; the spec now says so too.
- **Double-click:** double-clicking a tab still collapses the ribbon.
- **Old collapse state:** there's no more "first click expanded it" handling. If the app last closed collapsed, it opens straight into the new row.

**Code** (`src/ribbon.rs`): each command now has one entry in a list that records its tab, group and primary flag. It draws itself either large (expanded) or small (collapsed), so both views stay in sync and adding a command means adding one entry.

**Spec** (`spec/ui/components/ribbon/index.pi`): commands can be marked primary, all four currently are, and the collapsing section describes the new row.

**Test fix:** the ribbon test's check that the command area disappears when collapsed wasn't actually checking anything. The test tools couldn't see that element, so the check always passed. I made the ribbon's rows visible to the tests. The test now confirms that collapsing removes the tabs, shows all four commands in the row, and that expanding brings the tabs back.

**Still out of date:** the spec's newer group-title design (rotated up the left edge, with its own background) isn't built yet. The code still centres titles along the bottom.
